hierarchy.original_event: A motor vibrates steadily at 100 Hz for 1 second.

catalog.name: vertical_bounce
catalog.applicability: Passive vertical ball drop and repeated rebounds on a fixed flat surface. Not active dribbling or later rolling.

catalog.name: free_fall
catalog.applicability: Free vertical flight ending at first surface contact. No impact vibration is generated by this model; split off a subsequent impact when needed.

catalog.name: single_impact
catalog.applicability: One isolated normal impact against a fixed surface. Does not include repeated action or a separately described ringing tail.

catalog.name: sliding
catalog.applicability: Horizontal sliding/scraping with Coulomb kinetic friction; not rolling or actively changing applied force.

catalog.name: rolling
catalog.applicability: Horizontal rolling with effective constant rolling-resistance deceleration. No bounce-to-roll conversion is inferred.

catalog.name: damped_oscillation
catalog.applicability: One decaying ringing/vibration tail after excitation. The excitation impact itself must be separate if also requested.

catalog.name: periodic
catalog.applicability: Continuous steady periodic vibration of a motor/tool. Uses a sinusoidal carrier. Not a small count of distinct knocks.

catalog.name: stochastic
catalog.applicability: Irregular independent contacts such as sparse raindrops/gravel, represented by a Poisson process or its fixed-count conditional form.

catalog.name: rhythmic_action
catalog.applicability: Intentional repeated knocks/steps/taps, including active dribbling. Cadence is behavioral, not passive restitution.

decision.reason: The current action describes a motor vibrating steadily at 100 Hz for 1 second. This is a continuous, steady periodic vibration of a mechanical system (the motor), which matches the applicability and scope of the 'periodic' model exactly. The frequency (100 Hz) and duration (1 second) are directly specified in its parameters. No collision, sliding, or other physical regimes are involved; it is purely a sustained oscillation. The 'periodic' model is designed for continuous steady vibrations like this, using a sinusoidal carrier as described in its applicability. Other models such as 'single_impact', 'damped_oscillation', or 'rhythmic_action' do not fit: 'single_impact' is one-time and isolated; 'damped_oscillation' requires an excitation event and decaying tail, which isn't present here; 'rhythmic_action' implies intentional taps or knocks, not passive steady vibration. Thus, 'periodic' is the only model that fully covers this action without requiring splits or external assumptions.
